ap.notes: The 2026 hub could not be surfaced by search today (searches returned only syndicated AP copy). AP's 2024 free results hub was https://apnews.com/projects/election-results-2024/, so the 2026 equivalent is expected at the candidate URL, with topic hub https://apnews.com/hub/election-2026 (pattern, unverified). What is public: the apnews.com interactive results pages (HTML/JS; the JSON that feeds them is undocumented and unlicensed for reuse). What is not public: the AP Elections API (licensed, API key; results, race calls, county-level data) and AP's Google/partner feeds. AP race calls are what most outlets (NYT, NPR, PBS, Google) display.

nyt.notes: Not found by search today. Pattern from 2022 (/interactive/2022/11/08/us/elections/results-senate.html) and 2024 (/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-president.html); expect results-senate.html, results-governor.html, results-house.html and per-state pages such as results-ohio.html under /interactive/2026/11/03/us/elections/. NYT uses AP vote data and its own race calls/needle; the pages are HTML with undocumented JSON behind them; historically open on election night without a subscription.

ddhq.notes: URL taken from a Decision Desk HQ press release (https://ddhq.io/press/decision-desk-hq-releases-2026-congressional-forecast-model, dated July 15, 2026; fetched 2026-10-23); the /votes page itself was not fetched. DDHQ now uses ddhq.io for its main site and votes.decisiondeskhq.com for its 2026 forecast model and polls. DDHQ results data is a licensed product (clients include media outlets and financial firms); the public pages are free to view but the press release does not describe a public API. DDHQ also powers partner results pages (e.g., The Hill) in past cycles.
